speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth what is the estimated dollar value of the net economic return expected from Government grants and subsidies issued to pop singer Taylor Swift and her team, with the aim of motivating them to hold Swift's The Eras Tour concerts in Singapore in 2024.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth whether the Ministry is looking into ways to make concerts by marquee acts such as Coldplay and Taylor Swift in Singapore more inclusive and accessible for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Kallang Alive Sport Management (KASM), the entity that was put in charge of operating the Sports Hub after Government takeover, set out to be more than simply a venue for hire.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: KASM has a team which actively identifies and curates suitable content and programmes, and brings them into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Our aim is to bring a whole spectrum of events to Kallang for Singaporeans, from top-tier marquee events to community-related ones, and from music concerts to sporting and social events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There were some questions at takeover around whether the Sports Hub would be able to continue to attract top-tier events into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the last year, apart from the ongoing Taylor Swift concerts, we have brought in several world class acts, such as Mayday, Coldplay, Ed Sheeran and Jacky Cheung.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have also brought in marquee sporting events, including the FIBA Intercontinental Cup that came to Asia for the first time in 2023, the Super 750 Series Singapore Badminton Open, HSBC Sevens Singapore, WTT Singapore Smash, of which the third edition will begin sometime later this week, and innovative concepts, such as fitness racing series Hyrox.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the case of Taylor Swift, we moved fast and early to bring her show into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We did so as we recognised the large Swifties fanbase in Singapore and in the region and were keen to deliver the concert experience to them, right here at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The idea for A-list marquee events to be staged at the Sports Hub was conceived of even before the Government takeover in December 2022, as we recognised the tremendous upside of such concerts to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In February 2023, my colleagues and I from the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), SportSG and KASM went to the United States (US) to study the sport and entertainment industry.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When the opportunity to discuss holding a Taylor Swift concert in Singapore came up, we broached it immediately, subsequently discussed it in detail and, thereafter, reached an agreement for Singapore to be one of Taylor Swift’s tour stops.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We also saw the opportunity to make this a uniquely Singapore experience and it hence made sense to take a whole-of-Government approach and subsequently, other agencies, such as the Singapore Tourism Board (STB), were brought in.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: STB undertook its own assessment of the potential benefits of bringing the concert to Singapore and subsequently offered a grant to the concert promoter.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: STB assesses whether to give grants on a case-by-case basis, judiciously weighing up the benefits which might accrue to Singapore if the event was brought in.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The direct economic benefits include, for instance, additional tourist arrivals and additional spending on tickets, flights, hotel stays as well as entertainment, retail and dining in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Other cities which have hosted Taylor Swift concerts similarly reported an increase in economic activity arising from the concerts and we would expect the same in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Several market analysts have estimated a dollar range of the economic upside which we are likely to see from the staging of the concerts and whilst the event has not yet concluded, these may well be right.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, beyond the tourism and economic benefits, being able to host A-list artistes, such as Taylor Swift, will help position Singapore as a cultural hub in Southeast Asia, capable of hosting a range of different arts, music and culture events, as well as major sporting and lifestyle events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This helps to brand Singapore as a fun, vibrant destination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Straits Times noted, for instance, that the benefits include, I quote, “economic growth, cultural enrichment, to global recognition”, whilst Nikkei Asia reported that the concerts, I quote, “underscore the city-state’s growing status as a pop culture destination”.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Business Times also noted that these events made us, I quote, “look like a modern, open-minded and vibrant place”.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I would add that grants alone would not decide where a performer goes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Promoters of top artistes will do their own calculations and assess where they want to perform and for how long.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: One major consideration is the location, which is key.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are many reasons why world-class artistes choose to host large-scale concerts in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These include Singapore’s strategic location, quality infrastructure, good amenities, safety, efficiency and diverse cultural offerings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: KASM also proactively works with the artistes and promoters to make their experience of performing in Singapore a good one.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of this helps when attracting top-class events into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Singapore faces intense regional competition for these concerts and other such events, and we will need to continue investing in our infrastructure and software to continue attracting marquee entertainment, lifestyle and sporting events into Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It also extends to building Singaporeans’ affinity with the Sports Hub, as I said at the outset.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We are exploring ways for more Singaporeans from all backgrounds to enjoy marquee acts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On other occasions, we have also activated areas in the precinct to allow other members of the community to bask in the atmosphere.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This includes both entertainment events, such as the Taylor Swift concerts, as well as sporting events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, at the Singapore Smash 2023, we had community activations at the OCBC Square and also across the island with tables set up at 18 venues through Singapore whilst the main event was happening at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This provided Singaporeans with the opportunity to try their hand at table tennis and doing it on the same top-class tables that were used by the best players in the world.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Beyond marquee entertainment and sports events, KASM has a dedicated team that looks at delivering more community programmes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: While we cover a range of top-tier events that are ticketed, there are also non-ticketed and non-revenue-generating events, such as the large-scale festivals during Chinese New Year, Hari Raya and Deepavali.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This ensures that we have strong social return by providing programmes for everyone to bond, interact and build affinity with the Sports Hub.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I think the community really appreciates the work that has been done.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: So, for example, when Coldplay performed earlier this year, local musicians featured as opening acts; when Ed Sheeran performed in Singapore, he famously did a duet with JJ Lin and he also profiled a watch strap that was made by a local company.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: So, my question is, were similar cross-marketing opportunities contemplated when negotiating with Ms Swift's team and if not, is it something that the Government can keep in mind for future concert deals?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: My second question relates to the disclosure of the terms of the deal that was struck between Ms Swift's team and the Singapore Government.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: And if so, will the Government be taking any enforcement action against the relevant parties?

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai: I thank Ms Usha Chandradas for her comments.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: On her first question on cross-marketing, obviously, where possible, we would endeavour to do so.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: And that is why we have seen, in the case of Coldplay, having a local opening act.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In other cases as well, what we try and do on some occasion is, even if we cannot do it at the main event itself, at the periphery, on non-event days or in the lead-up or build-up to the A-list event that takes place in Singapore, we try to involve as many local artistes as possible.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The Member has brought up some examples, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In the case of artistes, very often the terms and conditions stipulate not just who is performing, their overall set-up, but also the opening act for each of the performers.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: So, in those cases, we will not be able to change the sequence or change the identity of the performers.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: But rest assured that when we can, we will endeavour to expose our local artistes to such platforms.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: First, I must thank the Minister for personally leading the Singapore delegation to Los Angeles to negotiate a deal to bring in The Eras Tour.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: I think that is a huge personal involvement on his part and I thank him for that.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: So, in line with that orientation and to my original question on whether there is a target for the total economic value-add from the concert economy that we are trying to grow in Singapore, could the Minister perhaps shed a bit more light on whether we should consider setting a more tangible target in terms of deal volume and deal flow, even if not economic value-add, the numbers that we expect to see from the concert economy that we are trying to grow in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He has raised an important point, but I think we should also set it in context.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When we first considered the idea of taking back the Sports Hub, there were questions around whether we had a team who would be able to engage with some of the world's top artistes and promoters.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Were we able to do this with large-scale crowds?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Not forgetting that, as we were embarking on these plans, we were still in the midst of dealing with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, when we looked at the plans overall, obviously, those are factors that had to be taken into account.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Eventually, I think it is important for us to work out a broader horizon, mid-term through to long-term, and understand where we want to go in terms of targets.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I want to stress to Mr Xie that, as I said at the outset of my answer, KASM is not trying to deal with the Sports Hub only for economic return.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To us, it is equally important that we have social return to the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To give the Member an example of how we have been able to achieve this, we work with top-tier marquee events, obviously high and good revenue-generating events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But in doing so and in making that revenue, we are able to plough it back into non-revenue-generating but highly impactful social events.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I gave the example of the National School Games taking place at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Almost three times the number of events compared to the best prior to COVID-19 days.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: All of that brings a certain feeling and resonance of school athletes to be playing at the top venue in Singapore at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I have given this example to the media as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Last year, we worked with the schools to stage the rugby finals right after the Singapore Sevens.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we had a pitch that was world-class.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We had a venue that was world-class, finished on Sunday with the finals.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On Monday or Tuesday, the schools stepped in.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And because we were able to host it without the financial restrictions in particular that we had before, we had 8,000 school children at the arena, at the stadium, supporting and cheering on their schools.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I was there and I think the feeling of camaraderie, the feeling of togetherness, being able to cheer your top athletes at such a forum is something that we value tremendously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these and other examples are what we want to go for, using the Sports Hub as a draw, as a vehicle and as an asset that the Government can use right across the spectrum and also combining it with non-Sports Hub facilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: For example, the rest of Kallang Alive, the precinct which I mentioned, there are parts which can be activated in support of and in tandem with the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, all these are the main motivations for KASM when they do their calculations for events for any particular given year.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am trying to move the Parliamentary Questions (PQs) along.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are still at the first set of PQs.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I will allow for a few more supplementary questions, but please keep them succinct and, likewise, replies to be succinct.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I assume he is answering the question that I filed for tomorrow as well.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And secondly, did the Government negotiate to make Taylor Swift's The Eras Tour the only blank space in Southeast Asia and did it realise that this may be perceived by some of our neighbours as being mean?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Giam filed a question for tomorrow with the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) on STB's position on grants.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I am not answering on behalf of STB.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the Member's two questions, well, let me deal with the second, which I think is also related to the first question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The real question is this: you have to make your calculations and work out what is in Singapore's and Singaporeans' best interests.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you do not have a certain economy of scale to play in Singapore over "x" number of nights for a period of time, you would not be able to reap the economies of scale.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Then, there is going to be a very different balance to the considerations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The concert might take place in Singapore but for far fewer nights, or it might not even take place at all in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, we have to look at the overall calculation and decide, for a particular event, what is the resonance with Singapore and Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We make this calculation overall and it is not in every case that we decide that we need to make a grant or we need to negotiate in a particular way.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Every event, whether it is lifestyle, sporting, arts, culture or music, has a different consideration.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We are motivated by different outcomes that we want to achieve.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, whether we shape it in one way, give a grant in another way or organise our framework to host the event in a particular way, all that is shaped by the outcomes that we want to achieve.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And then we also have to judge what is the demand that we have in the local market.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these, I hope, explain to Mr Giam some of the suite of considerations that we have in deciding how to approach this, which events to put a grant out to, on what terms, how to structure it and also taking into account the overall demand and objectives in Singapore.
